correctness.rationale: For all N>=2, exact integer coefficient identities express Q as alpha*C_N+(1-alpha)*C_{N-1} and yield two derivative recurrences. The Chebyshev-U derivative formula proves C_N and C_{N-1} have only simple unimodular roots; the recurrence excludes common roots. Phase-normalized boundary values then rule out unit-circle zeros for every 0<alpha<1. All finite roots move strictly outside at alpha=0, the extra degree-N-1 root begins at infinity, and continuous root count cannot change without a unit-circle crossing. The reciprocal recurrence gives exact first-order radial escape at alpha=1. Fu's compact-uniform kernel convergence plus strict polynomial exclusion proves local |s|<=t nonvanishing, only for non-endpoint alpha. The standalone Python checker passed 196 exact algebraic identities, 91 Chebyshev comparisons, 112 numerical root checks and 36 first-order velocities; no finite test is used to prove the infinite statements.

originality.rationale: Full-text statement-by-statement comparison establishes that the main 2026 seed gives the limiting polynomial, root number and angular concentration but not strict |z|>1 for all complex roots at each fixed exponent, nor the endpoint velocities. The exact same-object public real-root classification handles only negative real roots; the rational oblique palindromic theorem studies a different section. The inspected 1980 convex-combination theory assumes equal-degree monic endpoints. No stronger result with matching domain and implications was located. The residual possibility of older unindexed general root-stability theory is disclosed.
residual_risks: Older unindexed results on stable polynomials, self-inversive polynomials, and convex combinations of adjacent Chebyshev-derivative polynomials could imply the same exterior barrier; no absolute bibliographic uniqueness is certified.
Fixed-gap rational-Hartogs diagonal reports were compared at indexed statement level only; their different polynomial reduction makes coverage unlikely but the full texts were not all reviewed.

value.rationale: The natural singular-vertex rescaling of a recent Bergman kernel produces N-1 zeros; prior existence and angular concentration do not determine which side of the classical |s|=|t| scale every zero occupies. The theorem supplies an all-exponent, all-complex-root sharp exclusion barrier, with an exact nontrivial radial response at every endpoint root, and a rigorous zero-free local kernel core complementary to the known zero-producing region. This is a structural constraint on kernel zero geometry, not a small numerical enumeration or mere normalization check.
